measures.title: City of Lebanon police headquarters capital referendum
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Lebanon may increase property taxes paid to the city for up to 20 years to pay for designing, building and equipping a new police headquarters, including buying related land and related improvements. Principal debt would be no more than $52,165,000, with financing costs of no more than an additional $35,918,413, and the maximum annual tax amount could not exceed $4,454,550. The ballot estimates that the annual tax bill for a median $250,000 home would rise by $216 per year.
measures.yesMeans: The city may raise property taxes for up to 20 years to fund a new police headquarters.
measures.noMeans: The city may not raise property taxes through this referendum for a new police headquarters.
